newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Slovenia begs to be in first NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia begs to be in first NATO expansion.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek urged NATO on Tuesday not to overlook the small former Yugoslavian state when it embarks on its first expansion wave later this year.
Drnovsek said before addressing NATO ambassadors in Brussels it would be hard to explain to his people if Slovenia were excluded from a first intake of east European countries.
Of 12 former eastern bloc countries to apply, Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be the first to be invited to membership talks at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.

Strong doubts hang over Romania, despite strong backing from France, and while no serious reservations have been raised about Slovenia's ability to meet the criteria for joining, it lacks a major NATO ally strongly pushing its case.
"If it is about the criteria, about how ready is some candidate, then Slovenia must be accepted," Drnovsek told Reuters.
"If there is some other consideration, some new concept of strategic interest, then we could be out, but it would be difficult to explain then what is NATO enlargement about".
Among the criteria set by NATO are a stable market economy, democracy and human rights -- standards Slovenia is widely seen as having met.

Asked to come up with a more positive argument for Slovenia to be accepted, Drnovsek said that his country could provide a stabilising influence in the Balkans, as well as providing a land connection between Italy and prospective new member Hungary.
